# A private AI system: one builder, no team, real consequences.

Not a demo. One person builds and maintains it, and other people depend on it. It remembers from sources, coordinates across a household, and acts only inside the permissions it is granted. It runs across platforms and swaps models without a rewrite, so no vendor owns it, on hardware that cost less than a laptop.

[The point of view it shaped](https://etgarbonar.com/serviceable-line/)

The idea

## Not another chatbot. A personal system that works where life already happens.

This is a working pilot of a private operating system with long-term, source-backed memory. It connects knowledge and actions across the tools a person or family already uses, while keeping the system readable, inspectable, and portable.

I built it for three reasons: to experience first-hand, as an early adopter, how buying changes when AI does the finding, choosing and using; to run my own and my family's work and life on it; and to build differently. I have been a builder many times before. What is new is that I can now write the code myself: connecting systems and apps that were never connected, and automating processes that could not be automated before. Together with solving discoverability and selectability at Lokalise, it changed how I think product-led and sales-led motions evolve in the age of AI. It is now the platform, a second brain and its agents, that I use to assess where a company's serviceable line sits.

How it works

## Three ideas make it different.

01

### It remembers from sources

Important facts come from real notes, records, tasks, and logs. They remain traceable to their source instead of disappearing into vague conversational memory.

02

### It coordinates across life

Focused assistants connect personal administration, family and travel, household and finance, the connected home, and the flow of information between them.

03

### It keeps the owner in control

Access is scoped by task. Durable memory requires human approval, sensitive actions keep a confirmation step, and the knowledge remains readable outside any one AI model.

Seen in the system

## It remembers from sources, and the sources are connected.

Facts come from real notes, records and logs rather than from conversational memory. Each answer stays traceable to the file it came from, and the files reference one another.

Every bar in these captures is a deliberate redaction, not a rendering fault. What gets withheld follows a written disclosure rule, decided once, rather than a judgement call made page by page.

Where it works

## One operating layer for work and life.

Business work

Commercial strategy, AI visibility, product positioning, and decision support for confidential advisory work.

Personal administration

Inbox, calendar, tasks, documents, decisions, and project continuity.

Family and travel

Shared planning, groceries, trips, chores, allowance, and family coordination.

Household and finance

Vendors, receipts, payments, shared expenses, and recurring follow-ups.

Connected home

Lights, scenes, sensors, cleaning, watering, alerts, and household routines.

Health

Health records, test results, and history kept connected, organized, and searchable.

Operational evidence

## Built for real work, and run with the discipline it requires.

**Applied capability**

- Supports confidential advisory work in commercial strategy, positioning, AI visibility, and decision support
- Daily use through WhatsApp and Telegram, in English and Hebrew
- Source-backed memory plus connected tools and home systems

**Reliability**

- Nightly deterministic self-audits and canary checks
- Fallbacks across AI providers, with outage and recovery alerts
- Nightly offsite backups, a recovery runbook, and an incident log
- Watchers detect critical file replacement, session failures, and intrusion events, repair recoverable states, and alert when attention is needed

**Governance**

- Specialists receive only the tools their job needs
- The chores agent cannot inspect family photos because image access is not available to it
- Long-term memory, usage, and cost are reviewed on a defined rhythm

Multiple models, one governed system

### Model choice stays flexible. Usage stays visible.

Requests can move between providers when needed, while usage and cost remain measured by provider and every fallback stays visible. Subscriptions carry the work. Metered API billing is used only where no plan covers the job, which keeps it a deliberate exception instead of the default.

## Shared ledgers for chores, budgets, and tasks.

People report chores in the WhatsApp group they already share, where everyone can participate and see the result. The price list is fixed in advance, so what a job is worth is not renegotiated at the end of the week.

**Shared chores** WhatsApp group

What happened behind the conversation

**Pocket money, and an assistant that refuses to guess.** The familiar chat is only the surface. The important part is the rule-following behind it: verify the wording, ask when uncertain, then update the ledger deterministically.

Seen in the system

## It watches itself, and says so when something is wrong.

A health panel regenerates through the day across both the knowledge base and the machine underneath it. Alerts fire only on red, plus one message when a fault clears, so silence is meaningful.

![A status dashboard showing green checks for the knowledge base and its machine, plus one failed service in red. Product names, a service name, an address and an internal path are covered by opaque redaction bars.](https://etgarbonar.com/ai/assets/proof-status-panel.webp)

**The health panel, mid-day.** Backup freshness, credential checks, scheduled jobs, disk, memory, load and connectivity stay visible in one report. Here, one service is red while the rest remains healthy. That is when a WhatsApp alert fires, followed by one recovery message when the fault clears.

Trust by design

## Private enough to use. Inspectable enough to trust.

The operating system and its readable knowledge base run on a private home server. External AI models are interchangeable services, not the owners of the system or its memory.

Checks, incidents, and fixes remain visible. When a failure repeats, it is turned into a rule or a deterministic tool so the same problem is less likely to happen again.
